supporting_observations.claim: The domain account sysmaint was created by sam.okafor, then added to the Administrators group roughly two minutes later.

A task named Microsoft\Windows\HealthCheck was registered on WS-LMARTINS-01 by sam.okafor. Its encoded PowerShell command decodes to a hidden-window command that downloads and executes a script from http://203.0.113.250/a.ps1.
WS-LMARTINS-01 accepted an RDP logon for sam.okafor from 203.0.113.250. This is inconsistent with the stated practice that remote administration is only performed from WS-SOKAFOR-01.

The account name, administrator membership, and download-and-execute task do not match the stated help-desk practice for temporary accounts, which uses ext.<name> accounts without administrator rights.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records show task registration, but do not show whether the task ran or what the downloaded script contained.
The provided records do not establish who controlled the RDP source address or whether sam.okafor's credentials were compromised.
The records do not establish whether sysmaint was later used or whether its administrator membership was removed.
claims_not_established: The identity or intent of the person operating the RDP session.
Whether the PowerShell task executed successfully and what changes, if any, it made.
Whether the account creation and task registration were authorized through a process not included in the supplied context.
additional_evidence_needed: Task Scheduler execution history and PowerShell operational logs for the HealthCheck task.
The contents and hosting evidence for http://203.0.113.250/a.ps1, including proxy or network records.
Domain controller and endpoint authentication records that clarify the origin and authentication method for the RDP session and account changes.
Current and historical group membership, account usage, and any subsequent logons or actions by sysmaint.
Change approvals or administrator confirmation for the account creation, administrator-group addition, and scheduled task.
